one_line: A large-scale genome-wide association meta-analysis of clinical LOAD identifies five novel risk loci and implicates tau binding, APP metabolism, immunity, and lipid processing.
summary: This study performed a large genome-wide association meta-analysis of clinically diagnosed late-onset Alzheimer’s disease involving 94,437 individuals. The authors confirmed 20 previously known risk loci and identified five new genome-wide significant loci: IQCK, ACE, ADAM10, ADAMTS1, and WWOX. Fine-mapping of the HLA region confirmed the HLA-DR15 haplotype as a risk factor. Pathway analyses indicated involvement of immunity, lipid metabolism, tau binding proteins, and APP metabolism in LOAD pathogenesis. The findings demonstrate that genetic variants affecting APP and Aβ processing are involved in late-onset as well as early-onset autosomal dominant Alzheimer's disease.

key_claims.claim: Five new loci (IQCK, ACE, ADAM10, ADAMTS1, and WWOX) are associated with late-onset Alzheimer's disease risk.
key_claims.evidence: Genome-wide significant association (P ≤ 5 × 10−8) in a meta-analysis of 35,274 clinical/autopsy-documented Alzheimer’s disease cases and 59,163 controls.
key_claims.location: Results / Meta-analysis of Alzheimer’s disease GWAS

key_claims.claim: The HLA-DR15 haplotype is a risk factor for LOAD.
key_claims.evidence: Fine-mapping of the HLA region in 14,776 cases and 23,047 controls identified risk effects for the HLA-DR15 haplotype (FDR P = 0.013).
key_claims.location: Results / Fine-mapping of the HLA region

key_claims.claim: LOAD risk genes and pathways are enriched for rare variants.
key_claims.evidence: Highly significant correlation between common and rare pathway gene results (P = 1.32 × 10−7).
key_claims.location: Results / Candidate gene prioritization at genome-wide loci

methods.population: Clinically diagnosed late-onset Alzheimer's disease cases (n=35,274) and controls (n=59,163) of European ancestry

funding_and_conflicts: Funded by NIH and others. limitations: Rare causal variants may have been missed due to limitations in capturing all rare variants through imputation.
Some newly identified loci were analyzed in restricted sub-samples in Stage 3B.
